Copy the numbers from your soil test report. You don't need all of them: leave blanks for anything your report doesn't have. The translator explains each result and, just as usefully, tells you what you *don't* need to buy.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="st"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const PT = { olsen: [10, 20, 40, 'Olsen (sodium bicarbonate)'], bray: [15, 30, 60, 'Bray-1'], m3: [20, 45, 90, 'Mehlich-3'], ab: [4, 8, 12, 'AB-DTPA'] };
  const KT = { aa: [100, 175, 300, 'Ammonium acetate or Mehlich-3'], ab: [61, 121, 181, 'AB-DTPA'] };
  const band = (x, t) => x < t[0] ? 0 : x < t[1] ? 1 : x < t[2] ? 2 : 3;
  const TAG = [['bad', 'Low'], ['good', 'Medium'], ['good', 'High'], ['warn', 'Very high']];
  HM.tool({
    id: 'st', step: 'Your garden', units: false,
    inputs: [
      { k: 'use', l: 'What are you growing?', t: 'select', d: 'lawn', opts: [['lawn', 'Lawn'], ['veg', 'Vegetables or fruit'], ['beds', 'Flowers, shrubs or trees'], ['native', 'Native or low-water plants']] },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Results from your report' },
      { k: 'ph', l: 'pH', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'om', l: 'Organic matter (%)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'ec', l: 'Salts (EC or "soluble salts", dS/m or mmhos/cm)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'ecm', l: 'Salts method', t: 'select', d: 'paste', w: 3, opts: [['paste', 'Saturated paste (ECe)'], ['11', '1:1 or 1:2 water extract']] },
      { k: 'p', l: 'Phosphorus (ppm)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'pm', l: 'Phosphorus method', t: 'select', d: 'olsen', w: 3, opts: Object.entries(PT).map(([k, v]) => [k, v[3]]), h: 'Printed next to the result. Labs in alkaline regions often use Olsen or AB-DTPA.' },
      { k: 'k', l: 'Potassium (ppm)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'km', l: 'Potassium method', t: 'select', d: 'aa', w: 3, opts: Object.entries(KT).map(([k, v]) => [k, v[3]]) },
      { k: 'no3', l: 'Nitrate-N (ppm)', t: 'num', w: 3 },
      { k: 'lime', l: 'Free lime / carbonates', t: 'select', d: 'unk', w: 3, opts: [['unk', 'Not reported'], ['yes', 'Present (or "high" / soil fizzes)'], ['no', 'None']] }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const rows = [], todo = [], skip = [];
      const veg = v.use === 'veg', native = v.use === 'native', lawn = v.use === 'lawn';
      const calc = v.lime === 'yes' || (v.lime === 'unk' && v.ph >= 7.8);
      if (v.ph != null) {
        let t, m;
        if (v.ph < 5.5) { t = ['bad', 'Strongly acid']; m = 'Too acid for most lawns and vegetables; nutrients become less available.'; todo.push('Raise pH with ground limestone. Use the <a href="ph-adjustment.html">pH calculator</a> for the amount.'); }
        else if (v.ph < 6.0) { t = ['warn', 'Moderately acid']; m = 'Fine for many plants; lawns and vegetables prefer a little higher.'; if (!native) todo.push('Optional: a small lime application to bring pH toward 6.5. See the <a href="ph-adjustment.html">pH calculator</a>.'); }
        else if (v.ph <= 7.5) { t = ['good', 'Good']; m = 'Suits most lawns, gardens and landscape plants.'; skip.push('Lime or sulfur: your pH is already in the good range.'); }
        else if (v.ph <= 8.4) { t = ['warn', 'Alkaline']; m = 'Common in dry regions. Most adapted plants are fine; some (maples, pin oaks, blueberries, azaleas) develop yellow leaves from iron shortage.'; todo.push('Choose plants suited to alkaline soil. For yellowing between leaf veins on susceptible plants, use a chelated iron product (EDDHA type works in high pH).'); }
        else { t = ['bad', 'Very alkaline']; m = 'Above 8.4 often means sodium. Ask the lab for sodium (SAR or ESP) before planting.'; todo.push('Ask your lab to test for sodium.'); }
        if (v.ph > 7.5 && calc) skip.push('Sulfur to lower pH: soils with free lime neutralise it, so it takes huge amounts and rarely works. Grow plants that like your soil instead.');
        rows.push(['pH', HM.fmt(v.ph, 1), t, m]);
      }
      if (v.om != null) {
        let t, m;
        if (v.om < 2) { t = ['bad', 'Low']; m = 'Low organic matter means poor structure and less water and nutrient holding.'; if (!native) todo.push(lawn ? 'For lawns: core aerate and top-dress with ¼ in of compost; repeat yearly.' : 'Mix 1–2 in of compost into the top 6–8 in of beds. The <a href="materials-calculator.html?m=compost">materials calculator</a> gives the amount.'); }
        else if (v.om < 5) { t = ['good', 'Moderate']; m = veg ? 'Reasonable; vegetable beds do best around 5% or more.' : 'Fine for lawns and landscape plants.'; if (veg) todo.push('Add about 1 in of compost to vegetable beds each year.'); else skip.push('Compost or topsoil for soil improvement: organic matter is already adequate.'); }
        else { t = ['good', 'High']; m = 'Plenty of organic matter.'; skip.push('Compost, peat or "soil conditioner": you have plenty of organic matter already.'); }
        if (native && v.om >= 2) skip.push('Amendments for native plants: they generally do better without rich soil.');
        rows.push(['Organic matter', HM.fmt(v.om, 1) + '%', t, m]);
      }
      if (v.ec != null) {
        const e = v.ecm === 'paste' ? v.ec : v.ec * 2; // 1:1 roughly half of paste
        let t, m;
        if (e < 2) { t = ['good', 'Low']; m = 'Salts are not a problem.'; }
        else if (e < 4) { t = ['warn', 'Slight']; m = 'Sensitive plants (beans, strawberries, roses, some lawn grasses) may struggle.'; todo.push('Avoid salt-sensitive plants, go easy on manure and fertilizer (both add salts), and water deeply now and then to flush salts down.'); }
        else if (e < 8) { t = ['bad', 'Moderate']; m = 'Many garden plants will be stunted.'; todo.push('Leach salts with deep, slow watering if drainage allows; choose salt-tolerant plants; stop using manure and salty compost.'); }
        else { t = ['bad', 'High']; m = 'Most garden plants will fail.'; todo.push('High salts usually need drainage improvement and heavy leaching, or raised beds with imported soil. Check whether sodium is also high.'); }
        rows.push(['Salts', HM.fmt(v.ec, 2) + (v.ecm === 'paste' ? ' (ECe)' : ` (≈ ${HM.fmt(e, 1)} ECe)`), t, m]);
      }
      if (v.p != null) {
        const b = band(v.p, PT[v.pm]);
        const m = ['Low: plants may benefit from phosphorus.', veg ? 'Medium: adequate for most crops; vegetables may respond to a little.' : 'Medium: enough for lawns and landscape plants.', 'High: no phosphorus needed.', 'Very high: no phosphorus needed; extra washes into waterways.'][b];
        if (b === 0) todo.push('Apply phosphorus (the middle number on the bag) at the rate your lab suggests.');
        if (b >= 2 || (b === 1 && !veg)) skip.push('Phosphorus fertilizer, bone meal or "starter" fertilizer: phosphorus is already sufficient. Choose a product with 0 as the middle number.');
        rows.push(['Phosphorus', HM.fmt(v.p, 1) + ' ppm', TAG[b], m]);
      }
      if (v.k != null) {
        const b = band(v.k, KT[v.km]);
        const m = ['Low: plants may benefit from potassium.', veg ? 'Medium: adequate for most; vegetables may respond.' : 'Medium: enough for lawns and landscape plants.', 'High: no potassium needed.', 'Very high: no potassium needed.'][b];
        if (b === 0) todo.push('Apply potassium (the last number on the bag) at the rate your lab suggests.');
        if (b >= 2 || (b === 1 && !veg)) skip.push('Potash or "winterizer" fertilizers sold for their potassium: you have enough.');
        rows.push(['Potassium', HM.fmt(v.k, 0) + ' ppm', TAG[b], m]);
      }
      if (v.no3 != null) {
        let t = v.no3 < 10 ? ['warn', 'Low'] : v.no3 <= 30 ? ['good', 'Adequate'] : ['warn', 'High'];
        rows.push(['Nitrate-N', HM.fmt(v.no3, 1) + ' ppm', t, 'Nitrate changes week to week, so treat this as a snapshot. ' + (v.no3 > 30 ? 'High: skip nitrogen for now.' : lawn ? 'Lawns are fed on a regular nitrogen program regardless.' : 'Low values are normal before the growing season.')]);
        if (v.no3 > 30) skip.push('Nitrogen fertilizer for now: there is plenty in the soil.');
      }
      if (!rows.length) return U.empty('Enter at least one result from your report.');
      let h = `<table class="tt"><thead><tr><th>Test</th><th>Result</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead><tbody>` +
        rows.map(r => `<tr><td>${r[0]}</td><td>${r[1]}<br><span class="tag ${r[2][0]}">${r[2][1]}</span></td><td>${r[3]}</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody></table>';
      h += `<h3>What to do</h3>` + (todo.length ? `<ul class="plain">${todo.map(x => `<li>${x}</li>`).join('')}</ul>` : U.note('Nothing needs fixing based on these results.', 'good'));
      if (skip.length) h += `<h3>What you don't need to buy</h3><ul class="plain">${skip.map(x => `<li>${x}</li>`).join('')}</ul>`;
      h += U.note('Ranges vary between labs and crops. If your report gives its own categories or recommendations, those take priority.');
      return { html: h, work: [
        v.p != null ? `Phosphorus bands for ${PT[v.pm][3]}: low below ${PT[v.pm][0]}, medium to ${PT[v.pm][1]}, high to ${PT[v.pm][2]}, very high above (ppm)` : null,
        v.k != null ? `Potassium bands for ${KT[v.km][3]}: low below ${KT[v.km][0]}, medium to ${KT[v.km][1]}, high to ${KT[v.km][2]}, very high above (ppm)` : null,
        v.ec != null ? 'Salt bands (saturated paste, dS/m): under 2 low, 2–4 slight, 4–8 moderate, over 8 high. A 1:1 extract reads roughly half the paste value, so it is doubled for comparison.' : null,
        v.ph != null ? 'pH bands: under 5.5 strongly acid, 5.5–6.0 moderately acid, 6.0–7.5 good, 7.5–8.4 alkaline, over 8.4 very alkaline' : null
      ].filter(Boolean) };
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Getting a soil test

Most state university extension services run soil tests for home gardeners at low cost, as do many private labs. Ask for a **routine** or **garden** test: it usually covers pH, organic matter, salts, phosphorus, potassium and often nitrate.

- **Sample right.** Take 10–15 small cores from across the area, 0–6 in deep for gardens and 0–4 in for lawns, mix them in a clean bucket, and send about two cups.
- **Sample areas separately.** A vegetable bed, a lawn and a shrub border are different soils with different needs.
- **Every 3–4 years is enough** for most gardens, unless you're fixing a problem.

A soil test is the cheapest way to avoid buying fertilizer, compost or lime you don't need.
